stem: A student appears for a multiple-choice test with 8 questions. Each question has 4 options with exactly one correct answer. The student answers every question purely by random guessing. What is the probability that the student gets exactly 3 questions correct? [Given: (3/4)^5 = 0.2373]

per_option_rationale.rationale: 0.0586 = C(8,3)*(1/4)^3*(1/4)^5 = 56*(1/4)^8; the student used p=1/4 for both success and failure factors, ignoring q=3/4.
0.3164 = C(8,3)*(3/4)^3*(1/4)^5; the student swapped p and q, treating 3/4 as the success probability.
0.1406 = C(8,2)*(1/4)^2*(3/4)^6; the student applied the binomial formula for k=2 instead of k=3, computing P(X=2) rather than P(X=3).

explanation_sections.punchline: Identify the success probability as 1/4 (not 1/2) and use the given hint for (3/4)^5 to avoid lengthy computation.
explanation_sections.lesson: For multiple-choice guessing, p = 1/(number of options); remember to use q = 1 - p in the failure factor.
explanation_sections.timing: 75 seconds. C(8,3)=56 quickly; use provided (3/4)^5=0.2373. Main trap: swapping p and q.
